title: Anthropic AI Scanner Finds 77 Critical Open Source Vulnerabilities
summary:
A new security initiative from the team behind Claude aims to strengthen open source software through automated vulnerability detection. Known as OSS Scanner, the tool provides free, periodic scans using Anthropic's most powerful models for 114 projects accepted from roughly 650 applicants. Initial results identified 77 critical and 803 high-severity flaws, which are reported to maintainers alongside proofs-of-concept and potential patches.

Among the first findings was CVE-2026-92392, a high-severity memory-safety bug in curl that a project contributor described as one of the software's worst vulnerabilities in a long time. Anthropic continues to scan the remaining accepted projects to identify further risks, utilizing a methodology inspired by the OSS-Fuzz project to scale code auditing for the open source community.

A fix I'm excited about: curl, used by countless apps/devices to move data over the internet, just patched CVE-2026-92392. It's a high-severity memory-safety bug (a use-after-free) found with an early version of OSS Scanner.

@bagder called it one of curl's worst vulns in a long time, even if a crash is the likeliest outcome.

Thanks to Daniel and the curl team for fixing and writing it up so openly.

11 days ago, our team @AnthropicAI launched OSS Scanner to give open source projects free, periodic vulnerability scans from our strongest models, inspired by OSS-Fuzz. Some numbers so far:
• ~650 projects applied
• 114 accepted
• 77 critical and 803 high model-rated findings reported (we haven’t scanned all projects yet)
